core_obligations: Reduction to a vanishing differential (proof lines 6645-6662): writing the page E_r as the direct sum of its even and odd parts, the differential provides maps in both directions whose composites vanish, and the displayed computation in the K-group identifies the alternating class of E_r with that of E_{r+1}; all intervening objects lie in the smallest weak Serre subcategory containing the components of E_r, and since only finitely many components are nonzero the operation may be iterated until the differential vanishes.

The identity (proof lines 6663-6667): at the stage where the differential is zero, each cohomology object has a finite filtration, supplied by the convergence lemma, whose graded pieces are exactly the components of the page in question, so the alternating sum of the classes of the cohomology objects equals the alternating sum of the classes of those components in the K-group of the smallest weak Serre subcategory.
Finiteness (proof lines 6655-6667): the finiteness of the support is inherited by the later pages, and the argument shows that only finitely many cohomology objects are nonzero.
proof_roadmap: Compare the alternating classes of two consecutive pages using the even and odd parts.
Iterate until the differential vanishes, staying inside the smallest weak Serre subcategory generated by the components.
Use the finite filtration on each cohomology object to read off the identity.
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that for a filtered complex with finite filtrations and only finitely many nonzero components on some page, only finitely many cohomology objects are nonzero and their alternating sum of classes equals the alternating sum of the classes of the components of that page, in the K-group of the smallest weak Serre subcategory containing them (statement lines 6629-6642). The proof is a complete argument: the alternating class of a page is shown to agree with that of the next page by splitting into even and odd parts and using the differential (proof lines 6645-6655), the reduction may be iterated because the support stays finite and all objects involved stay in the same weak Serre subcategory (proof lines 6655-6662), and at the stage where the differential vanishes the finite filtration on each cohomology object gives the identity (proof lines 6663-6667). The non-formal content is the iterated class computation. The claim is H2: a structured argument with each input named.
